correct_completion: I would have passed the exam by now.
full_sentence: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam by now.
acceptable_variants: I'd have passed the exam by now.
I would be a doctor now.

options.text: I passed the exam last year.
options.why_wrong: This is a finished past event. It does not match the hypothetical past condition in the 'if' clause or the present result signalled by 'by now'.

options.text: I would have passed the exam by now.
I will pass the exam next week.
options.why_wrong: This is a real future plan. A mixed conditional needs a hypothetical result based on an unreal past condition.

options.text: I pass the exam every term.
options.why_wrong: This describes a habit in the present. It does not express the imagined result of an unreal past condition.

grammar_focus: Mixed conditionals: past perfect in the 'if' clause with 'would have' plus a present time expression in the main clause
explanation: The stem uses 'if' with the past perfect, which describes an unreal past condition. The main clause uses 'would have' plus the past participle, linked to a present result, so the time phrase 'by now' is needed. Spanish speakers often use a simple past or a simple conditional here because Spanish marks this kind of hypothetical meaning with different verb tenses, so the English pattern needs to be learned as a fixed form.
translation: Si hubiera estudiado más, ahora habría aprobado el examen.
